findings.issue_text: [BUG] The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test issues xhr :put to remove_member, but the only route wired to remove_member is DELETE 'members' (routes.rb), so the PUT matches add_members instead. The PUT request routes to Admin::GroupsController#add_members, where params.require(:usernames) raises ActionController::ParameterMissing, returning a 500 — the spec's expectation of 422 fails, so the shipped test suite is red and the automatic-group guard for remove_member is never actually exercised.

[BUG] The members template iterates {{#each m in members}}, but after this diff removed afterModel and _members from group-members.js.es6, nothing ever sets a 'members' property on the members controller — findMembers stores members on the group model, not the members-route controller. The user-facing group members page (route group.members) renders an empty table for every group, because 'members' resolves to undefined on the members controller; admins can see the list but regular users navigating /groups/:name/members get nothing.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which yields 2 pages when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members with limit 50 → totalPages 2, but only one real page exists). showingLast is false on the last populated page, so the admin clicks 'next' and fetches offset 50 of 50 members, receiving an empty member list with the pager showing 2/2 — the admin group page dead-ends on a blank page for any group whose size is an exact multiple of its page size.

[ADVISORY] remove_member deletes rows via group.users.delete(user_id) directly on the association collection, bypassing the GroupUser model's destroy callbacks and the Group#remove path used elsewhere. Any logic that runs when a user leaves a group (e.g. automatic group title removal / group-user observers) is silently skipped, so admins removing members via the new UI leave stale titles and derived state behind; the next maintainer changing GroupUser lifecycle will not realize this controller sidesteps it.

[ADVISORY] findMembers returns undefined (bare 'return ;') when the group name is empty, while every caller (setupController in both routes, next/previous actions) either fires it without a promise or returns it as an action result. Callers that previously relied on the resolved-promise contract (the removed afterModel chaining, and the next/previous actions which return the value to Ember's action handling) get undefined; currently nothing crashes, but the empty-name early-exit path is untested and any future .then on findMembers' result will throw.

[BUG] The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test issues xhr :put against an endpoint whose only route is delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member'. The PUT does not match any route, so the request raises an ActionController::RoutingError before reaching the controller; the test never exercises remove_member's automatic-group guard (response is a routing failure, not the asserted 422), so the guard on the delete path is unverified.

[BUG] {{#unless automatic}} is evaluated against the member (Discourse.User) item context, which has no 'automatic' property, not against the group. 'automatic' is always undefined inside the each-item view, so the remove link renders for every member of automatic groups; an admin clicking it triggers DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members for an automatic group, which the server rejects with 422 while the UI promised a removable member.

[BUG] totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing an extra page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit. For 100 members with limit 50, totalPages is 3; clicking next on page 2 fetches offset=100, the server returns an empty member list, and the admin sees '3/3' with a blank member panel.

[BUG] add_members silently skips usernames that do not match any user and still renders success_json. An admin who typos a username gets a success response, the member list reloads unchanged, and no error is surfaced anywhere — the added-member verification this refactor's own spec deleted ('succeeds silently when adding non-existent users') had at least asserted the no-op; now neither the server, the client, nor any test covers the failure feedback, so the admin believes the member was added.

[BUG] remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) followed by group.save, but the diff removes the patch-based incremental delete path (update_patch) that the old specs verified ('can make incremental deletes', 'succeeds silently when removing non-members') without any replacement coverage for non-existent user_ids. The new DELETE endpoint has no spec for removing a user who is not a member (or a non-existent user_id), so a regression in GroupUser join-row deletion would ship unnoticed; group.save on an association mutation is also a no-op placeholder that hides whether deletion actually failed.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten members endpoint (new meta envelope with total/limit/offset, default limit 50, and pagination applied to non-automatic groups for the first time) has no controller spec in this diff. Every client consumer — the admin pagination UI in admin-group.js.es6 and the public group-members route — depends on result.meta.total/limit/offset existing and on offset semantics matching currentPage's Math.floor(offset/limit)+1; a serializer or param-handling regression here breaks both the admin pager and the public members page with no test failing.

[ADVISORY] addMembers leaves the usernames input populated after a successful add (the code's own TODO), and addMembers supplies no failure handling for the PUT that removeMember also lacks. An admin resubmits the form and re-adds the same usernames, or, on a server 422 (e.g. adding to an automatic group if the template guard from the automatic finding is hit), the UI gives no feedback while the input retains stale text.

[ADVISORY] findMembers returns undefined (bare 'return ;') when the group name is empty, while all call sites (admin route setupController, group-members route, removeMember/addMembers reload) treat it as a promise. Any caller that chains .then on findMembers (the deleted afterModel pattern, or future reload chains in removeMember's '.then(function() { self.findMembers(); })' successors) crashes with a TypeError for a nameless record; the old code returned an RSVP.resolve so the contract silently changed.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips nonexistent usernames and its render_json_error branch is dead code, so admin adds of typo'd usernames produce success with zero feedback. An admin pastes a wrong username, the server returns success_json, the member list reloads without the user, and there is no error anywhere — the admin cannot tell why nothing happened; the group.save error path can never fire because group attributes were never modified.

[ADVISORY] The public update action drops the previously-supported params[:group][:usernames] membership payload with no deprecation, silently accepting PUTs that no longer change membership. Any out-of-tree client or script doing PUT /admin/groups/:id with group.usernames gets a 200 success while memberships are silently unchanged — a silent public-surface behavior change not traceable to any stated requirement.

[BUG] The '.remove_member cannot remove members from automatic groups' spec issues xhr :put against a route defined only as delete "members" => "groups#remove_member", so the request cannot reach the action. The spec raises an ActionView::MissingExactRoute/ActionController::RoutingError (or hits an unintended route) and fails, meaning the automatic-group guard for removal is not actually tested by this suite.

[BUG] The {{#unless automatic}} guard around the remove link evaluates the `automatic` property in the member (User) context, where it does not exist, so the guard is always true. The remove × link is rendered for automatic groups' members in the admin UI; clicking it triggers removeMember, the server returns 422, and the admin sees a remove affordance that can never work — the automatic-group invariant is enforced only server-side and contradicted by the UI.

[ADVISORY] The members endpoint applies no bounds on the client-supplied limit/offset, accepting arbitrary values such as limit=1000000 or negative offset. A client (the new pagination UI or any API consumer) can request an unbounded member serialization, turning the new pagination feature into a full-table dump and defeating the page-size invariant the change was supposed to enforce.

[ADVISORY] addMembers never clears the usernames input and no failure handling exists on addMembers/removeMember promise chains, so the stated membership-management intent is only half-implemented. After a successful add, the typed usernames stay in the selector; clicking Add again re-adds the same users, and a failed PUT/DELETE (e.g. 422 on automatic groups) leaves the UI showing the stale member list with no error message.

[BUG] The public /groups/:name/members endpoint changes its response shape from a bare array of serialized members to {members: [...], meta: {...}} with no versioning. Every existing API consumer (Discourse's API is public; plugins and external integrations reading the members list) parses an array today and receives an object after this diff, breaking member lookups for all of them; the diff simultaneously drops the PATCH-based incremental update path, so there is no compatible way to manage memberships via the old contract.

[BUG] The frontend members page (discourse/templates/group/members.hbs) has no pagination controls, but this endpoint now unconditionally caps results at limit 50. For any group with more than 50 members, members 51+ become unreachable on the public group members page (previously the full list was rendered for non-automatic groups); admins and users silently see a truncated roster with no indication anything is missing.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which produces an extra page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit. A group with exactly 50 members and limit 50 reports totalPages 2; showingLast is false on page 1 so the next link is enabled and navigates to an empty page 2 (offset clamped to user_count, server returns 0 rows), leaving the admin staring at a blank member list.

[BUG] The `automatic` guard in group_member.hbs resolves against the member item context (a Discourse.User), not the group, and User has no `automatic` property. The remove ('x') link renders on every member row even when viewing an automatic group; clicking it issues DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members which the server rejects with 422, so the admin gets an unexplained error on a control that should never have been shown.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips any username that does not match an existing user (User.find_by_username returns nil and the iteration continues), then reports success_json. An admin who typos one of several usernames gets a success response and a reloaded list missing that user with no error, so the failed add is invisible unless they recount the roster; the old PATCH path had the same flaw but this diff enshrines it in the new dedicated endpoint.

[ADVISORY] removeMember/addMembers reload via findMembers at the unchanged offset, and findMembers clamps offset with Math.min(user_count, ...) against the possibly stale pre-remove user_count. Deleting the last member of a page leaves offset equal to the old user_count, so the reload returns an empty page while earlier members exist (admin must click previous to see anyone); any mid-page removal shifts subsequent members so one row is skipped from the displayed page.

[ADVISORY] findMembers changed its empty-name contract from resolving [] to returning undefined, and callers (both route setupController hooks) fire it without handling the promise. Any future caller that chains .then on findMembers (as the old routes did) gets a TypeError on the no-name path since the sentinel now means 'not loaded' rather than 'empty list' — the semantics change is unguarded by any caller update in this diff.

[BUG] PUT /admin/groups/:id silently drops the usernames payload: the old update_put honored payload[:usernames] (and raised 403 for automatic groups), but the new #update reads only params[:alias_level], params[:visible], and params[:name], discarding params[:group][:usernames] without any error or deprecation. Any existing API client (or plugin) that edits group membership by PUTting {group: {usernames: ...}} now receives 200 success_json while its membership change is silently discarded — the admin UI was updated to the new /members endpoints, but every out-of-tree caller silently no-ops and loses member edits with no signal.

[BUG] The PATCH branch of the update action (update_patch, handling params[:changes][:add]/[:delete]) was deleted, so PATCH /admin/groups/:id now falls through to the PUT code path, which finds no :alias_level/:visible/:name/:group params and just calls group.save on an unchanged group. A client that issues the previously supported PATCH with changes: {add: username} gets a 200 success response while zero membership changes occur — an incremental-add API turned into a silent no-op instead of a 410/404, so membership drifts out of sync with what the admin believes happened.

[BUG] The save action's else-branch now calls group.create() with no usernames, so the controller's user-typed usernames are never transmitted during group creation, whereas the old flow called createWithUsernames(this.get('usernames')). An admin who types usernames into the selector before first saving a new group loses those entries: create() ignores usernames, the new group is saved with zero members, and no error or re-prompt appears — the input the user explicitly provided is silently dropped (the template also hides the add-members UI until id exists, so there is no path that preserves it).

[BUG] The per-member template gates the remove link on {{#unless automatic}}, but inside the group-member view the context is the member (a Discourse.User), so 'automatic' resolves against the user record, is undefined, and the link renders for automatic groups too. Admins viewing an automatic group (e.g. admins/moderators) see a working remove icon on each member; clicking it triggers DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members which the server rejects with 422 can_not_modify_automatic, surfacing an error after the fact instead of never offering the action — the old UI correctly disabled member editing for automatic groups.

[BUG] The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route (config/routes.rb delete "members" => "groups#remove_member") only allows DELETE, so the request fails on routing/method mismatch rather than reaching the 422 automatic-group guard it claims to verify. The test either errors on the unmatched PUT route or passes for the wrong reason; the actual automatic-group protection in #remove_member is never exercised, so a regression that removes the can_not_modify_automatic guard would not be caught by this spec.

[ADVISORY] The public endpoint /groups/:group_id/members changed its response shape from a bare serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}} with no versioning, deprecation, or format negotiation. Every existing consumer of the endpoint (themes/plugins, API integrations iterating the top-level array) breaks immediately on deploy; the core frontend was updated in the same diff, but external consumers get a hash where they expect an array and render zero members or crash.

[ADVISORY] add_members splits params[:usernames] on ',' with no whitespace stripping (usernames.split(",").each { User.find_by_username(username) }), whereas the previous update flow went through the group's usernames= setter which normalized input. An admin pasting 'bob, alice' (with a space after the comma) causes ' alice' to not be found; the loop skips it silently and the endpoint returns success_json, so the admin believes both members were added when only the first was — a silent partial failure.

[ADVISORY] The members endpoint accepts an unbounded, unvalidated user-controlled limit parameter ((params[:limit] || 50).to_i with no upper cap) and performs a full group.users.count on every request. An anonymous client (this is the public /groups/:group_id/members.json route, gated only by ensure_can_see!) can pass limit=2000000000 to make the serializer iterate every member of a large group, and hammer the endpoint to force a COUNT(*) over a large join table per request — a cheap amplification/DoS vector against any site with large groups; the old code capped automatic groups at 200.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips usernames that do not resolve to a user (if user = User.find_by_username(username) returns nil the name is dropped with no error or feedback) and then reports success_json. An admin who pastes a list with a typo'd or since-renamed username gets a 200 success response while the membership was never applied — the intended user silently lacks group privileges (or, for a removal workflow, retains access the admin believes was revoked), with no signal in the UI or logs to detect the gap.

[ADVISORY] The .update context only tests the automatic-group name-ignoring path; the deleted test 'is able to update group members' was not replaced by any positive test for updating a normal group via the new flat parameter shape (params[:name]/params[:alias_level] instead of params[:group][:name]). A regression in Admin::GroupsController#update for non-automatic groups (e.g. the param-shape change breaking name/alias_level/visible updates, or group.save failing) passes the entire suite because the only update tests exercise automatic groups; every admin editing a normal group gets silently broken updates.

[ADVISORY] The new .add_members endpoint's behavior of silently skipping non-existent usernames (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb, `if user = User.find_by_username(username)`) has no test — the old incremental tests 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' were deleted rather than ported to the new action. A future change that raises on unknown usernames (or the opposite, that adds users by partial match) is undetected; admins adding a misspelled username get a success response with the member silently absent, and the suite says nothing either way.

[ADVISORY] The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test issues `xhr :put, :remove_member` although the route added in config/routes.rb is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, so the test's request verb does not match the route the frontend actually uses (DELETE). Because controller specs invoke the action directly, this test passes regardless of the HTTP verb routing; a regression in config/routes.rb (e.g. the DELETE member route being removed or repointed) leaves this suite green while the admin UI's remove button 404s. Checked files: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb is the only test file in the diff and it contains no routing-level (request/integration) assertion for these endpoints.

[BUG] add_members splits usernames on "," without stripping whitespace and silently skips users not found, so comma-space separated input ("a, b") adds only the first user while still returning success_json. An admin pasting "user1, user2" into the selector gets a success response and a reloaded list missing user2; members silently fail to be added with no error surfaced, unlike the old update_put path which went through group.usernames= (which handled parsing via the model layer).

[BUG] The remove_member specs call xhr :put, :remove_member while routes.rb only declares delete "members" => "groups#remove_member", so the specs exercise a nonexistent PUT route and raise ActionController::UrlGenerationError instead of testing the actual endpoint. The suite fails (or, if the framework were lenient, the real DELETE endpoint ships completely untested); the production client (group.js removeMember, type: "DELETE") hits a code path no spec ever covered.

[ADVISORY] The PUT /admin/groups/:id endpoint silently dropped support for the group[usernames] membership payload that update_put previously accepted, and create dropped group[usernames], with no deprecation period. Any existing API consumer (scripts, plugins, admin-adjacent tooling) that synced membership via PUT create/update now receives success_json while its membership changes are silently discarded — the group is saved with no membership change, a silent no-op on a previously functional public API.

[ADVISORY] totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing a phantom page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and showingLast on that page. An admin paging a 100-member group with limit 50 sees "1/3"; clicking next lands on an empty third page where next is still not disabled, and the previous "showingLast" guard never fires on the real last page when offset math drifts.

[ADVISORY] create strips the group name ((params[:name] || '').strip) but update does not (group.name = params[:name]), so the same value round-trips differently through the two endpoints. An admin who edits an existing group and submits a name with trailing whitespace bypasses the normalization create applies; the rename either fails validation with a confusing error or, if validation is whitespace-tolerant, leaves a group whose name differs from what the admin thinks they saved.

[ADVISORY] findMembers returns undefined (bare return) when the group name is empty, whereas the previous implementation returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]), breaking any caller that chains .then on the result. The group-members route's previous afterModel chained on findMembers' promise; any remaining caller that does group.findMembers().then(...) (the pattern the deleted route code used) throws a TypeError on new/unsaved groups, and the empty case no longer produces the empty member list the old contract promised.

[BUG] add_members silently skips unknown usernames and returns success_json, reporting success while dropping the requested work. An admin who typos a username (or pastes a user who was renamed/deleted) gets a 200 'success'; the member is never added and no error message or log identifies which username failed, so the admin believes the membership was granted and downstream permissions (e.g. private category access) are silently missing.

[BUG] removeMember and addMembers call self.findMembers() inside .then without returning it, so a failure of the member-list reload is an unhandled promise rejection that leaves the previously rendered member list in place with no error surfaced. After a successful add/remove, if the follow-up findMembers request fails (network drop, 500), the admin still sees the pre-operation member list — e.g. a removed member still appears after a confirmed removal — with no error dialog; the rejection also propagates as an unhandled promise rejection.

[BUG] setupController fires model.findMembers() as fire-and-forget with no rejection handler and no guard for the undefined return when the group name is empty. If the members request fails (403 for hidden group, 500, network error) the admin group page renders with an empty/missing member list and zero user feedback; the rejection is unhandled and the failure is indistinguishable from a group with no members.

[BUG] The addMembers action neither returns the model.addMembers promise nor has any in-flight guard or input clearing, so concurrent invocations interleave and the committed input state desyncs from the server. Double-clicking the Add button issues overlapping PUT requests; and because the username input is never cleared after a successful add (the TODO), the same usernames remain in the selector and are re-submitted on the next click, while the controller gives the caller no promise to observe success/failure — a failed add leaves the input populated as if it had been consumed.

[BUG] remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) then group.save and returns success_json even when the user was never a member, and group.save is a no-op on an unchanged record so validation cannot report the miss. A request with a stale or wrong user_id gets a 200 success while no membership was removed; the admin UI (which reloads the list and trusts the response) treats the no-op as a confirmed removal, hiding the real state from the operator.

[BUG] totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, overshooting by one page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit, so showingLast is never true on the boundary page. For a group of exactly 100 members with limit 50, page 2 of 2 displays as '2/3' with the next arrow enabled; clicking next advances offset to 100 and renders an empty member page reported as '3/3', so the admin sees a phantom empty page and the last-page guard never engages.

[BUG] findMembers returns undefined (bare 'return ;') when the group name is empty, and the request itself is fired before result.meta is validated — the caller awaiting it (previously the route's afterModel) now receives undefined instead of a promise. Any caller that chains on findMembers() for an unnamed group gets undefined and crashes with a TypeError on .then; on the meta path, if the response lacks meta (server error shape change), result.meta.total throws inside the then handler, surfacing as an unhandled rejection rather than a user-visible error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing a phantom page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and showingLast on that page. An admin paging a 100-member group with limit 50 sees "1/3"; clicking next lands on an empty third page where next is still not disabled, and the previous "showingLast" guard never fires on the real last page when offset math drifts.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100/50), this yields 3 instead of 2, creating a phantom last page. The `next` action uses `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, so on the “real” last page it advances `offset` to `user_count` (e.g. 100), and `Group.findMembers` then requests `offset=100`, which the server will return as an empty page (`limit 50 offset 100`). Because `showingLast` is based on `currentPage == totalPages`, it will be false on the real last page, allowing navigation into the empty phantom page.
